resolved_source_locations.conclusion: This paper isolates a control-stable intrinsic family inside the fixed-support recombination layer of Six Birds theory. The first three papers of the series established admissible event packages on fixed support, predictive quotients on single histories, and the branchwise and recombination quotients on branch assemblages. Here we identify a two-anchor relative-cycle family in which branchwise predictive agreement does not determine later recombination observables. We instantiate the standard factorized no-interference collapse on the flagship surface, exhibit exact-finite separation for two flagship anchors, and formalize a concrete Lean witness kernel for the reference-positive anchor, including a no-factorization corollary. We separate the flagship positives from classical mixture, hidden predictive memory, protocol artifact, and boundary-collapse or completion-sensitive negatives using an explicit matched control bundle. We also show that nearby exact positives exist within the same relative-cycle family, while the erasure side remains empirical support rather than formal core.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: The contested program. The most anticipated near-term probe of quantum gravity is the BMV proposal (Bose et al.; Marletto–Vedral) : place two masses in spatial superpositions, let only gravity couple them, and test whether they become entangled. The widely-stated inference is that gravitationally-induced entanglement would witness a quantum (coherent) gravitational mediator — a graviton-like degree of freedom. The fork of §5.2 forces the opposite: the gravitational arm is a sibling readout that does not have access to the quantum phase mode and cannot carry it coherently between parties.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: This appendix collects the formal definitions and theorem statements used in the main text. At the level of general mathematical form, the quotient and factorization language used here sits near behavioral equivalence, bisimulation, exact aggregation, and standard quotient-factorization arguments . It does not reproduce proofs. The comparison base is inherited from the first three papers of the series: fixed support and admissibility, the current and predictive quotients on single histories, and the branchwise and recombination quotients on branch assemblages. The present paper uses those inherited structures only to define and compare the flagship recombination family on a common exact-finite support. At the single-history level, the current quotient Q_i identifies reachable histories that are indistinguishable by the current event package, while the predictive quotient M_i identifies histories that remain indistinguishable under all admissible future generator/observable words on the reachable image. At the branch-assemblage level, the branchwise quotient K_i identifies assemblages with the same weighted multiset of predictive classes, while the recombination quotient R_i identifies assemblages that are indistinguishable by admissible later recombination observables. When recombination equivalence refines branchwise equivalence there is a canonical forgetful map _i : R_i → K_i .

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: We study recombination-sensitive branch structure on a fixed-support substrate in Six Birds Theory. Building on prior work on event packaging and predictive holonomy, we introduce branch assemblages and two quotient levels at an interface: a branchwise predictive quotient ( K_i ), which captures independent predictive treatment of the branches, and a recombination quotient ( R_i ), which captures admissible recombination observables on branch families. On this architecture we exhibit a benchmark suite separating classical mixture, hidden predictive memory without recombination sensitivity, route-marked suppression, erasure-conditioned recovery, cyclic-family generalization, dissipative washout, and artifact controls based on protocol internalization and flattening/completion. A supporting theorem layer proves the abstract factorized no-interference regime and its obstruction by strict refinement, and one promoted positive family is connected to a theorem-backed concrete witness in an aligned Lean model. We do not claim a general reconstruction of non-Hilbert interference or a formalization of the full benchmark runtime. The claim is narrower: these recombination phenomena arise on fixed support, can be audited exactly, and admit a partial formal backbone on the Six Birds substrate.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: Foundations IV is a catalog of layer-agnostic structural laws built on the Foundations I/II/III apparatus. Its organizing question is what must be true, before choosing a substrate—whether analysis, arithmetic, physics, biology, chemistry, economics and finance, linguistics, cognitive and social science, or computation—for a layer to have lawful access, stable records, transport, symmetry, closure, and limits. The contribution is a uniform normal-form template applied across 52 laws; each row states its setup, theorem, proof spine, case structure, interaction status, and nonclaims, so recurring obstructions such as failed descent, hidden predictive structure, local-global failure, and record nonclosure can be compared in one register. The formalization status is explicit: the catalog contains 46 direct Lean theorems, 2 substrate-delegated anchors (No-Needles Stability and Closure–Reality Boundary), 2 partial wrappers (Hiddenness and Duality Fixity), and 2 obligation wrappers (CSL Formed-Closure and Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking); the four trust-base axioms used by the wrappers are disclosed through an opacity-guard pattern, each guarded by an opaque source predicate that prevents the axiom from being instantiated without the corresponding substrate or future-source certificate. Foundations IV is not a foundational reset of Foundations I/II/III, not a unification claim about the eight axes, and not an exhaustive catalog.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: The program's open problems are not vague: each is a named lemma or audit with a stated success criterion. (i) The L60 → L64 lemma — mass-closure charge-linking forbids a second neutral record channel — upgrades Prediction 3 to an all-structures law. (ii) The F43 continuum audit — tower-coherence, cofinality, residual-vanishing, completion — either licenses the continuum Einstein limit of the discrete consistency condition or names the exact obstruction. (iii) Exact RT saturation in the large-bond limit (the 0.729→0.904→0.941 trend made a theorem with a rate). (iv) Uniqueness of the grounding: whether semiclassical co-sourcing is the only admissible warrant for the common carrier (warranted → forced). (v) A third substrate for the universality thesis — the atlas's remaining foreclosure edges (black-hole thermodynamics and singularities are the natural candidates) — turning n=2 into n=3 with the genre-expectation again stated in advance.
